lawyer: Md Ozhillah with Ellius Ahmad, Advocate—For the Petitioners.
parties:
Mokter Hossain (Md) and others ------- Petitioners
vs
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others --------- Respondents
full_judgment:
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents No. 1-4 to show cause as to why the impugned Order No. 4 dated 6-7-2017 in Miscellaneous Review No. 01 of 2017 passed by the Learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, and Vested Properties Return Appellate Tribunal Kushtia. Accepting the application Annexure-F filed against Judgment and Decree dated 26-5-2016 (Decree being signed on 30-5-2016) passed by the learned Vested Property Return Appellate Tribunal, Kushtia in Vested Property Appeal No. 31 of 2015 affirming the Judgment and Decree dated 12-8-2015 (Decree being signed on 16-8-2015) passed by the learned Vested Property Return Tribunal, Kushtia in Vested Property Suit No. 305 of 2013 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 3. Background leading to the Rule, in short, is that one Ramjan Ali who is the predecessor of the petitioners Md Mokter Hossain and others filed a suit bearing No. 2305 of 2013 before the District Judge and Vested Property Tribunal challenging the government decision and to free his land from the schedule "Ka' of vested properties and the Suit was tried accordingly by the Vested Property Return Tribunal as Vested Property Return Suit No. 305 of 2013 and after recording the evidence and hearing the argument of the parties the learned Judge passed Judgment and Decree on 12-8-2015 in favour of the plaintiff and ordered Deputy Commissioner of Kushtia to submit a report within 30 days to the Tribunal after transferring the possession of the land in question in favour of the predecessor of the petitioners namely one Ramjan Ali. And against the said order the respondent No. 3, the Deputy Commissioner, Kushtia being aggrieved filed an appeal before the Vested Property Appellate Tribunal, Kushtia being No. 31 of 2015. The appellate Tribunal affirmed the Judgment and Decree passed by the Vested Property Tribunal dated 12-8-2015. Meanwhile, Ramjan Ali who is the predecessor of the petitioners died during the pendency of the Appeal and the present petitioners were added as a party and the said decree was made in their names as legal heirs of said Ramjan Ali by the Judgment and Decree dated 26-5-2016. Thereafter, the government decided not to file any writ petition against the Judgment and Decree passed by the Vested Property Return Appellate Tribunal. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the decision of the Appellate Tribunal, Bangladesh Government, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Kushtia filed Miscellaneous Review on 8-6-2017 before the Vested Property Appellate Tribunal, Khustia being No. 01 of 2017 which was admitted and by the order dated 06-7-2017 the Additional District Judge, 1st Court and Vested Property Return Appellate Tribunal, Kushtia accepted the application (Annexure-'F') filed against the Judgment and Decree as aforesaid against which the petitioner moved this Division under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule and order of stay. 

 5. In elaborating his submissions the learned Counsel has drawn our notice to section 4 of the -3rf-4-z,ion,Zook" read with section 22 of the same and submits that the "অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন, ২০০১" is a special law and it has specifically made Civil Procedure Code applicable where the said Ain itself has mentioned the same to be applied and also in case of section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure that is res-judicata, the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable. He further submits that section 22(3) has made the decision of the Appellate Tribunal final and therefore, review is not maintainable in such proceeding. The respondent Government, if so advised, may find its remedy under Article 102 of the Constitution but no review particularly lies against the Judgment and Decree passed by the learned Tribunal and affirmed by the Appellate Tribunal. 

 13. Here, it would be profitable if we bring some analogy from another discipline of law that is Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 just for better understanding and appreciation of the whole thing. In Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which is also a special law in section 5(2), 6(1) section 26 and so on, Code of Civil Procedure has found it's place that is in other words in so many places of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain the Application of Code of Civil Procedure has been specifically ensured, of course in a limited form. Even then by judicial pronouncement of both the divisions it has been settled that in Artha Rin Ain no review lies. In the decision of Sultan Alam @ SA Badal vs Rupali Bank reported in 46 DLR 292 considering long line of the decisions on the point the Appellate Division and this Division decided that the review is not permissible against the judgment and decree of Adalat. This view also finds support in the decision of Abdus Samad vs Sonali Bank, 9 BLC 554. His Lordship Justice Iman Ali while considering the same issue observed: 

 "We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates, perused the petition and affidavit-in-opposition. Clearly the decision reported in 46 DLR 292, is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the case since that case involved the review of the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat, for which the Ain provides the right of appeal. We are of the view that since the Ain does not provide any remedy by way of review of an order of Adalat the provision of Order XLVII, rule I will be amenable for the purpose of review and earlier order of Adalat." 

 14. On the conspectus, the irresistible result that follows is that we unhesitatingly hold that the acceptance of review application by the order impugned against (Annexure-'F') was without jurisdiction since no review lies against the Judgment and decree passed by the Vested Property Return Appellate Tribunal.
